# Copper Scroll Column 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Copper Scroll Column 1 (treasure locations 1-4) where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 1:1 — ruin/ruins

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "In the ruin" — singular, matching Hebrew chorvah |
| LOGOS | "In the ruin" — singular form preserved |
| PNEUMA | "Among the ruins" — plural for natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted singular "in the ruin" per EMET/LOGOS. The Hebrew is singular chorvah; PNEUMA's plural is interpretive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:2 — steps/staircase

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the steps leading to the east" — literal ma'alot |
| LOGOS | "the steps that lead eastward" — formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "the eastern staircase" — compact dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the steps leading eastward" combining EMET's literal "steps" with LOGOS's "eastward." PNEUMA's "staircase" is a reasonable interpretation but adds specificity not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS blend.

---

## 1:3 — vessels vs. contents

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a chest of silver and its vessels" — literal kelim |
| LOGOS | "a silver chest together with its vessels" — reordered |
| PNEUMA | "a silver chest with its contents" — dynamic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a chest of silver and its vessels." The Hebrew kelim means vessels/implements, not generic contents. PNEUMA's "contents" loses the specificity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 1:5-6 — tomb-monument/funerary monument/memorial tomb

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "In the tomb-monument" — hyphenated nefesh |
| LOGOS | "In the funerary monument" — formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "In the memorial tomb" — dynamic reordering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "funerary monument" as the clearest rendering of nefesh in its Mishnaic sense of a tomb marker structure.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:6 — course/row/layer

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "course of stones" — architectural term |
| LOGOS | "row of stones" — standard English |
| PNEUMA | "layer of stonework" — dynamic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "course of stones" per EMET. "Course" is the correct architectural term for a horizontal row of masonry.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 1:7 — ingots/bars

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "one hundred ingots of gold" |
| LOGOS | "one hundred gold ingots" |
| PNEUMA | "a hundred gold bars" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "one hundred gold ingots" per LOGOS word order. "Ingots" preferred over "bars" as more precise for cast metal. LOGOS word order is more natural in English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:9 — cistern/water tank

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the great cistern" — literal bor |
| LOGOS | "the large cistern" — formal |
| PNEUMA | "the great water tank" — explanatory |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the great cistern" per EMET. "Great" better matches the Hebrew gadol than "large," and "cistern" is the standard rendering of bor.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 1:10 — covered/concealed/hidden beneath

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "covered with sediment" |
| LOGOS | "concealed by sediment" |
| PNEUMA | "hidden in a hollow in the floor beneath silt" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "covered with sediment" per EMET as the most literal. PNEUMA's restructuring moves "hollow" into this line but it belongs earlier. "Sediment" preferred over "silt" as closer to the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 1:13-14 — master/lord/ruler + nations/peoples/foreign nations

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "master of the nations" — literal ba'al ha-goyim |
| LOGOS | "lord of the peoples" — formal variant |
| PNEUMA | "ruler of foreign nations" — interpretive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "master of the nations" per EMET. Ba'al is literally "master/owner." PNEUMA adds "foreign" which is not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 1:14 — sacred vestments/holy garments

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sacred vestments" — bigdei qodesh |
| LOGOS | "sacred vestments" — same |
| PNEUMA | "holy garments" — simpler register |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sacred vestments" per EMET/LOGOS consensus. "Vestments" carries appropriate liturgical weight.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:17 — rendered unclean/declared ritually impure

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "rendered unclean" — literal nitma' |
| LOGOS | "which has been rendered unclean" — expanded |
| PNEUMA | "declared ritually impure" — interpretive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "rendered unclean" per EMET. The addition of "ritually" by PNEUMA is interpretive though accurate. LOGOS's relative clause is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

*Total disagreements in Column 1: 11*
